findings.title: forEach with async callback is not awaited, breaking error handling and ordering
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) is used inside a try/catch block. Array.prototype.forEach does not wait for async callbacks, so any error thrown inside the async callback (including from the newly-async getCalendar call) becomes an unhandled promise rejection rather than being caught by the surrounding try/catch. Additionally, the outer function can proceed (e.g. to sending emails) before calendar/video deletions actually complete, since forEach doesn't return a promise. This should use Promise.all with .map instead of forEach.

findings.title: Same forEach(async ...) issue as vital/reschedule.ts
findings.body: Identical to the vital reschedule.ts issue: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...}) inside try/catch does not propagate errors into the catch block and does not block execution until the async deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls resolve, since getCalendar is now async. This can silently swallow calendar/video deletion failures and proceed to send reschedule emails before cleanup finishes.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) means booking cancellation side effects are not awaited
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...) ... }) is not awaited by the caller. Since getCalendar is now async, the loop fires off promises that are not tracked, so sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the webhook dispatch further down can run before the calendar/video deletions complete, and any errors from these async calls become unhandled rejections instead of being surfaced.

findings.title: Dynamic import() at module top-level still eagerly loads every app at startup
findings.body: The appStore object's values are the results of calling import("./appX") directly as object literal properties. These import() calls execute immediately when the appStore module is evaluated (object literals evaluate all their values eagerly), so every app package is still loaded eagerly at process startup, exactly as before, just now wrapped in Promises. This defeats the stated purpose of the PR (async/lazy imports) while adding await overhead at every call site (getCalendar, getVideoAdapters, payment app lookups, etc.) without actually deferring any loading or enabling code splitting benefits. A lazy factory, e.g. appStore[app] as a function returning import(...), would be needed to truly delay loading until first use.
